MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 25, 2022
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Bucknum
at 5:01 p.m., on October 25, 2022, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on October 20, 2022, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Goodell (arrived at 5:03 p.m.)
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Labor Negotiators Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6(a):
  Agency Negotiators: City Manager Dennis Wilberg; Assistant City Manager Keith
  Rattay; City Attorney William Curley; Human Resources Manager Monique Goetz;
  Labor Attorney Peter Brown: Employee Organization: Service Employees’
  International Union (SEIU)

Robert Breton, M.V.: Spoke on his gratitude to the City Council and Staff. He pointed out how the
City Manager and Assistant City Manager on how their vision has taken us to the promised land.
Criticized the current lawsuit as petty and strictly for partisan political purposes.

City Council Minutes  1  October 25, 2022
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:07 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley stated that there was one labor negation closed session and council gave
direction but no reportable action.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclamation of the Council of the City of Mission Viejo Supporting the Iranian-
  American Community and Condemning the Violence Perpetrated by the Government
  of Iran Against Its People

  Presented proclamation to Shani Moslehi.

P2. Presentation for the Honorees at the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce Women in
  Business Event

  Presented certificates of commendation to Visionary of the Year, Carmen Stramara on behalf
  of Cristina Gamarnik, owner of The Mommy Center; Advocate of the Year, Lauren Becker,
  Regional Director at Braille Institute; Resilience Award, Kateryna Karasyk, Managing
  Director of Elephant Signage & Display; Owner of the Year, Kelly Uygan, Blue Moon Pilates;
  and Founder of the Year, Jane Parmenter, Co-Founder of Parmenter Insurance.

P3. Proclaim November 26, 2022, To Be Small Business Saturday

  Presented proclamation to Chamber of Commerce CEO Doug Zielasko.

P4. State Legislative Updates

  Received presentation from Cori Takkinen of Townsend Public Affairs.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Henny Abraham, Costa Mesa: Spoke out against the atrocities in Iran and encouraged all cities to
support the Iranian community. She thanked the City Council for their support.

City Council Minutes  2  October 25, 2022
 Robert Breton, M.V: Spoke in support of the City Council under the distractions that they are facing
and praised their calm and dignified presence. Stated there is no bad findings in this lawsuit.

Bill Moorhead, M.V.: Introduced himself as Board Member of Moulton Niguel Water District and
outlined his accomplishments and asked for your vote. He announced his website is
Moorehead4water.com. and supports Donald Froelich and Diane Rifkin for the Moulton Niguel
Water Board.

Diane Rifkin, Laguna Niguel: Introduced herself as a Board Member on Moulton Niguel Water
District and outlined her experience. Asked for her vote and supports Bill Moorhead and Donald
Froelich.

Donald Froelich, Laguna Hills: Introduced that he is VP of Moulton Niguel Water District and is
running for re-election and asked for his support. Voiced concerns of the current drought situation.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated that the City Council is a disgrace and the City Attorney should be
disbarred. Recapped the current lawsuit. Encouraged voters to visit MissionViejoGuardian.com.

David Rynerson, Huntington Beach: Spoke in favor of SolarAPP+ for online permitting for
residential solar panels. Stated that there are grant opportunities.

Bob Ruesch, MV: Announced he is running for City Council in District 1 and asked residents in
District 1 to vote for him. He outlined his experience on the Planning Commission and what he
has accomplished during his term.

Lamar Kirchhevel, Laguna Hills: Spoke on SB 379 that requires cities to streamline rooftop solar
online permitting. SolarAPP+ from the US Department of Energy is a no cost option for cities
through limited grants. Encouraged the City to complete the grant application so residents have an
easier time pulling permits.

Ed Maurer, M.V.: Spoke on renewable energy and is in favor of SolarAPP+.

Emma Walker, Huntington Beach: Spoke in favor of SolarAPP+ for online permitting for
residential solar panels. She recapped cities that currently have this online permitting system.

Connie Lanzisera, M.V.: Spoke on item #11 and had various question to staff. Voiced concerns on
the cost to the City.

Terri Aprati, M.V.: Announced that she is running for City Council in the 4th district and asked
residents in her District to vote for her. She outlined her goals if elected. She encouraged that we
work together and to be non-partisan.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Spoke out against the three Council Members for illegally holding office. He
recapped the lawsuit. Criticized the Chamber of Commerce Council Forum held last Wednesday.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Spoke on the specific plan for the Village Center and suggested ideas.

City Council Minutes  3  October 25, 2022
 Ken Golemo, M.V.: Announced that he is running for District 4 as a write-in candidate. He observed
that while he has been canvassing the large part of his district didn’t understand district voting.
Asked for help on his and his wife’s self-published children’s book to be read at the Library. He
ended his comments in a prayer.

Michelle O’Brien, M.V.: Stated that she loves everything about Mission Viejo. Questioned that
during the candidate forum not one candidate had any new ideas. She praised on how the current
Council along with Rancho Santa Margarita Water District were able to get more water in Lake
Mission Viejo. She commented on the partisan lawsuit. Voiced outrage on the person who stole her
flag, pole and the mounting from her home.

Wendy Lee, M.V.: Commented that Mission Viejo is one of the safest cities in the U.S. and safest
schools. Voiced concerns of the newly adopted laws from the State Legislature on housing. She
stated it’s more important now to have a City Council that will fight to keep the State in check. She
praised the current City Council.

Linda Shepard, M.V.: Announced that she is running in District 1 for City Council. She outlined
her qualifications and requested your vote. Stated her website is electlindashepard.org Spoke out
against abortion and asked residents to vote no on Proposition 1.

Rebekah Earnest, M.V.: Thanked the City Council for their service and complimented the slope
maintenance and special events throughout the City. She spoke on the current condition of the
Garden Center and the disrepair it is in and voiced concerns on this center.

Mayor Bucknum asked that staff bring back information on SolarAPP+ at a future meeting.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 11 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve the
Consent Calendar outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the regular City Council Minutes for the meeting of October 25, 2022, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated September 23, 2022 in the Amount of $980,441.78

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  4  October 25, 2022
 3.  Check Register Dated September 30, 2022 in the Amount of $1,735,159.14

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated October 7, 2022 in the Amount of $4,543,088.04

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2022

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for August 2022

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2022

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for August 2022

  Received and filed.

9.  2021 Residential Resurfacing-Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 22838)-Notice
  of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of recordation
  of the Notice of Completion; and (5) approved Change Order No 1 to GMU Geotechnical,
  Inc. for $23,879.

10. Janitorial and Related Services at City Facilities and Recreation Centers

  (1) Approved Eighth Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Alliance Building
  Maintenance, LLC, and (2) authorized a Change Order to the existing Purchase Order for
  Alliance Building Maintenance, LLC, in an amount not to exceed $150,000.00.

City Council Minutes  5  October 25, 2022
 12. Amending the City of Mission Viejo Salary Schedule

  Adopted Resolution 22-41 Amending the City's Salary Schedule Effective January 1, 2023.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

11. Civic Center EV Charging Stations - CIP 22249

  By consensus the City Council directed staff to continue this item to the next council meeting
  with more information on the maintenance cost and the charge for electricity that will be
  distributed.

NEW BUSINESS

13. Proposed Ordinance Adopting the 2022 California Building and Fire Codes, the
  International Swimming Pool and Spa Code and the International Property
  Maintenance Code

  City Attorney Bill Curley gave a brief report and Building Official Paul Melby and OCFA
  Fire Marshal Lori Smith gave updates to the Building and Fire Codes.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to (1)
  introduce Ordinance 22-346 Adopting by Reference the 2022 Editions of the California
  Building, Residential, Plumbing, Electrical, Mechanical, Green Building Standards,
  Historical Building, and Existing Building Codes, and the 2021 Editions of the International
  Swimming Pool and Spa Code and International Property Maintenance Code, Together, with
  Certain Appendices and Amendments Thereto, and Amending Title 8 of the Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code; (2) introduce Ordinance 22-347 Adopting by Reference the 2022 California
  Fire Code, Together with Certain Amendments and Deletions; and (3) schedule a Public
  Hearing for December 13, 2022 to adopt the Ordinances identified in (1) and (2).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

14. Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  No report was given.

15. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Goodell.
City Council Minutes  6  October 25, 2022
 16. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Council Member Raths.

17. Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Kelley.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay presented a report on Parks and Facilities Improvement
Projects Update.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

City Attorney Curley stated that the Court of Appeals has put a Stay on all actions, the Council
remains in office as valid office holders, you are not removed. The Court of Appeals is looking to
see if the trial court process was correct or if there was prejudicial error.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell mentioned that he attended Laguna Niguel’s State of the City, the
Association of California Cities – Orange County (ACCOC) Fall Conference in Huntington Beach,
the Montanoso Grand Opening, the Library Gala, and Principal for the Day at Newhart Middle
School. He stated he will attend the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)Finance and
Administration committee meeting this week.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley alerted the community that there will be an event on Thursday 6:00 pm in
the Council Chamber on the history of the Mission Viejo Library by Robert Breton. Commented
that she has met with Code Enforcement and a resident regarding the Garden Center. She stated
she attended the Tee It Up for Marines Golf Tournament at Camp Pendleton. She highlighted the
Walk Against Drugs and gave kudos to Police Services. Council Member Kelley participated as
Principal for the Day at Bathgate Elementary School. She also attended the Pumpkin Diving Event
and the Dia de los Muertos event at the Potocki Center. Council Member Kelley noted that she left
the Candidate Forum early to attend the Capistrano Unified School District meeting to advocate for
City Council Minutes  7  October 25, 2022
 the Capistrano High School Football Stadium renovation. She commended the Superintendent
Kirsten Vital Brulte, Deputy Superintendent Clarke Hampton, along with Board Members Gila
Jones, and Judy Bullockus for their support and advocacy for this stadium. She noted that it did
pass unanimously. Lastly, she stated that this Election has brought out the worst in people and that
there is a lot of hit pieces being sent out. She encouraged resident to contact her if they hear or see
anything that looks questionable.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked the Mayor for presenting the proclamation this evening to the
Iranian American Community. He stated that he joined the Board of Directors of the Flying
Leatherneck Aviation Museum which is being shut down in Miramar. It will now be moved to t
the Great Park in Irvine. He announced that Saddleback Valley American Legion Post 862 and 281
have merged and there will be a fundraiser at The Bistro K in Laguna Niguel on November 13 from
1pm to 4 pm. Council Member Raths congratulated the Women in Business awards. He stated he
also attended the Montanoso Grand Opening and Tee it Up for Marines at Camp Pendleton, along
with Principal of the Day at Castille Elementary School.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs introduced and welcomed our new Fire Division Chief Cheyne Maule and
thanked Baryic Hunter for the work he did as an interim Fire Chief.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum commended Police Chief McDonald on the Walk Against Drugs. Emphasized
how great of an event this is every year. She congratulated the City’s successful events and asked
if the Library could get Mr. Golemo’s book read at the Library. Council Member Bucknum stated
that the Mission Viejo J.V. Golf Team participated in the Under-Amour Women of Will Golf
Tournament at the Oso Creek Golf Course. She announced that the Jr. Nationals and the Nationals
for diving will be in Mission Viejo next year. She stated that the best form of government is the
government that is closest to you, not Sacramento and this is why she serves on regional boards.
Lastly, she read from a letter from a Montevideo 4th grade student and quoted from Proverbs,
“Whoever walks in integrity walks securely”.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:41 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting Tuesday, November 8, 2022.

______________________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
